speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a history involving gait and limb ataxia; to understand the underlying cause, please describe your specific symptoms, when they started, and if there is any family history of neurological conditions. Also, have you noticed any issues with your vision, speech, or coordination?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing that; the "drunken" gait and right-sided clumsiness suggest a cerebellar or brainstem issue. Has this ataxia been progressive over time, or did it start suddenly? Additionally, do you experience any double vision, slurred speech, or difficulty swallowing?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That history is critical. The combination of Crohn's disease and natalizumab use raises a high suspicion for Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). Have you noticed any new visual changes, weakness, or sensory loss in the past few weeks?

text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy. The MRI findings of multifocal demyelinating lesions without enhancement are classic for JC virus reactivation in an immunocompromised host with a history of Crohn's disease.
